Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned on the dedicated-capacity validation you requested.

Recap (what you told us)
- Workload: multi-tenant customer support assistant + routing classifier. Typical prompt length ~220 tokens, responses ~120 tokens.
- Traffic profile: weekday peak ~200 concurrent users generating ~2k requests/minute, steady-state ~40 rps.
- SLO targets: p95 latency for streaming responses <= 150 ms (server-side token latency), end-to-end response (first byte) <= 250 ms for short responses; sustained throughput to support 200 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming: required — client consumes token-by-token; connection timeouts are strict (idle ~30s).

What Redwood proposes for validation
1) Reserved capacity test on Dedicated with two GPU profiles: H100 (80GB) and A100 (80GB) to compare sustained throughput and p95 streaming latency.
2) Validation plan: synthetic load + replay of sampled production prompts (we’ll use obfuscated payloads), run 3 x 10-minute sustained-steady tests and 2 x 1-hour soak tests under target concurrency.
3) Metrics we’ll measure: p50/p95/p99 token latency, first-byte latency, tokens/sec aggregate, GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV-cache hit rates, fail/retry rate.
4) Sizing recommendation: start with reserved throughput equivalent to ~250 rps baseline (buffers headroom for bursts) and test autoscale/burst behavior.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft sizing sheet and a copy of the SLA template for review.

Next steps (please confirm):
- You: confirm the two customer prompts set to replay and any additional constraints we should know about (e.g., PII handling window, on-prem traffic routing).
- Redwood: provision temporary Dedicated nodes (H100 and A100) and share validation plan + scripts. Estimate: we can run initial comparisons in ~5 business days after signoff.
- Schedule: propose Wed 21 Oct or Thu 22 Oct for the initial validation run; please confirm availability for a 60-minute window.

If that all looks right I’ll loop in infra and lock the time.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this summary looks accurate. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Prompts: we’ll send an S3 link with 1k de-identified production prompts by EOD today. Please confirm you’re OK with S3-hosted input and that Redwood will not persist raw prompts beyond the test window.
2) Latency: p95 <= 150 ms for token emission is our internal target for the chat experience; first-byte <=250ms is a hard requirement.
3) Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming clients is the sustained goal; we’ll also want to validate short spikes to 350 concurrent for 2–3 minutes.
4) Compliance: we need to ensure logs for the test are retained for 90 days and that any artifacts are provided to our security team for review.

Wed 21 Oct works for Tom and me; Thu 22 Oct is also ok if you need the extra time. Please go ahead and provision both GPU flavors and share the test harness so our infra can be on standby.

Thanks Marissa / Samantha — added some technical notes inline and a proposed test matrix:

Key technical assumptions:
- Model: open-llm-13b (quantized paths q4_0 and q8_0) for parity tests. We'll also run a high-accuracy fp16 H100 run to understand headroom.
- Sequence lengths: worst-case 1024 to validate KV cache behavior; typical 350 seq should be our primary metric.
- Networking: expect 10 Gbps host NIC in Dedicated; we’ll validate with 25 Gbps where available.

Proposed matrix (short):
- H100 (fp16) — reserved throughput: baseline 250 rps, concurrency stepped: 50/150/200/350 (short spike) — measure token p95/p99.
- A100 (q4_0 & q8_0) — reserved throughput: baseline 250 rps, same concurrency steps — measure throughput per GPU and memory headroom.
- Cache on vs off — to quantify prefix hit benefit for repeated conversational context.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ensure first-byte metrics.

Data retention: logs/summaries retained 90 days; raw prompts removed after validation unless Finovate requests otherwise (we will get documented permission).

I’ll prepare the harness (k6 + custom token-streamer) and push to the shared drive today. Rafael, please confirm GPU instance types and any infra quotas we need to lock.

- Aditya
